9/24 中美会晤：提前关注几个潜在交易方向
9 月 24 日 Trump–Xi 华盛顿会晤，会有AI 芯片、稀土/关键材料、关税和农业采购几个具体议题。推演下

1. AI 芯片与出口管制。 目前 AI competition 已经进入双方讨论范围，包括先进 GPU 对华出口、AI 模型和AI safety 等。如果 H200 之后进一步放宽 GPU 对华销售，最直接关注 NVDA、AMD，其次是 AVGO、MRVL、DELL、SMCI 等 AI 基础设施链。不过这一项也是谈判难度最大的，不能提前假设一定会放宽。

2. 稀土和关键材料。 如果中国进一步放松 InP（磷化铟）、镓、钨、钇等关键材料的出口限制，对半导体和光通信供应链的风险溢价会下降。尤其 InP 本身就是高速光模块激光器的重要材料，所以这里可以重点观察 LITE、COHR、AAOI、AXTI等。

3. 关税。 双方目前还在讨论部分非战略商品降低关税和延长贸易休战。如果出现实质性进展，最大的意义是降低中美贸易战重新升级的 tail risk，对整个 risk-on 环境更友好，消费电子、工业、半导体和中国供应链敞口较高的公司都会受益。

农业采购和 Boeing 也可能被谈到，对 ADM、BG、DE、MOS、BA 等可能形成事件驱动。

Last 3-4 days in the Indian market have been crazy.
Sharp down. Sharp up. Down again. Up again. Atleast that's what happening in my portfolio 

This is exactly why I am big proponent of having two portfolios: Core and Swing.

My Swing portfolio ~35% , When the market cracked, my SL got hit and I exited.  That part of the portfolio moved to cash by default 
The remaining 65% was in my Core portfolio. None of those stocks gave me a weekly close or fundamental exit, so I did nothing.

Within the next couple of days, most of the drawdown in the Core portfolio had already recovered.

So,Here's the learning.

In a choppy market, swing trades will get stopped out. That's completely fine. That's the system doing its job.
The problem is this.
Once you are sitting in cash, it's very difficult to time re-entry if your entire portfolio in Swing. The biggest reversal day usually comes when you're still waiting for confirmation in cash.
That's where Core helps.

It stays invested through the noise and participates in the recovery and some part of your portfolio sees those big reversal which that many complete swing traders miss.

I know I’m a week late, but I often don’t know what to say about this stuff and try to stick to trading. But 9/11 really was such a visceral experience for anyone living around NYC. This story from @lmaschler is incredible. Just watch it.

It transports me right back. I remember being in school. No true grasp of what was occurring, no cell phones. Parents were running in crying to pick up their kids and a friend’s mom told me that my dad was alive. It didn’t even hit me that he might not be. Other kids in my school weren’t so lucky. What a defining moment in our collective memories. Just like Covid lockdowns.

A crazy full-circle part of this story: Lee and Trillium took on a handful of traders displaced by 9/11. One of those traders went on to become their #1. That trader trained me and made me the trader I am today.

I am sure most of you saw the SEC’s innovation exemption today, but the CFTC also released something important that may have gone under the radar: 

Partial protection for software developers, an issue many viewed as central to the CLARITY Act.

In practice, providers of “passive software,” including qualifying self-custodial wallets and trading interfaces, can allow users to access CFTC-regulated markets without being required to register as introducing brokers.

To qualify, the developer must remain genuinely passive: it cannot custody user assets, generate explicit buy or sell signals, exercise discretion over order routing or execution, or otherwise control the user’s trades. The transactions must also take place through CFTC-registered exchanges, brokers or futures commission merchants.

This expands the relief previously granted specifically to Phantom and makes it broadly available to qualifying software providers.

It is important, however, not to overstate it. This is a CFTC staff no-action position, not legislation, and it does not provide the comprehensive developer safe harbor contemplated under the CLARITY Act. It does not resolve potential DOJ or FinCEN liability under federal money-transmission laws, bind the SEC or state regulators, or necessarily protect developers operating interfaces for unregistered DeFi markets.

Still, alongside the SEC’s announcement, it shows that regulators are already using their existing authority to implement meaningful pieces of the framework that Congress failed to pass.
